tier_reason: Peer-reviewed PVLDB 19(5):958-972 (2026) paper with public artifact repo (NTU-Siqiang-Group/ArceKV; prod branch tools/arce_bench, dev branch examples/arce_dynamic_compaction_integration.cc) and stated hardware (i9-13900K), but neither the paper nor the READMEs state a compiler version or flags (README only says gcc/g++ with a CMake Release build), so it cannot be A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Paper: average 2.00x and 1.41x over 1-Leveling (RocksDB's default compaction style, the strongest baseline) across the two dynamic workloads; 2.17x-2.92x over Tiering and LazyLeveling; around 3x faster than state-of-the-art compaction strategies in dynamic scenarios; over 10x vs Cassandra and WiredTiger and 3x vs Pebble. Repo README (prod branch, in-memory tmpfs variant vs RocksDB leveling): total latency 282.09s vs 808.85s at read_ratio 0.1 (2.87x) shrinking to 438.04s vs 479.20s at 0.9 (1.09x) (derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated in paper; repo README lists gcc/g++ (version unstated) with a CMake Release build
corrections.caveats: The paper states no compiler or flags. The 1-Leveling/Leveling/Tiering/LazyLeveling baselines were implemented on the RocksDB-based Moose framework, not stock RocksDB builds. Stock RocksDB appears only in the industrial-system comparison. The default 'prod' branch is explicitly NOT a faithful implementation of the paper: it is an in-memory adaptation for a TikTok recommendation service. An on-disk version was published on the 'dev' branch (2026-04-29), and its README reports a modest gain over leveled compaction: 1.41x total runtime (929.0s vs 1310.5s) and about 10% lower all-op latency, with worse insert latency (2.45us vs 2.15us) and higher compaction I/O. The prod README's cmake line has a typo (-CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE). License: GitHub detects GPL-2.0; the tree carries RocksDB's COPYING (GPLv2), LICENSE.Apache and LICENSE.leveldb.

notes: The paper is real and peer-reviewed (PVLDB vol 19 issue 5, 2026, not VLDB 2025 as recorded), and the headline numbers match its text. The tier drops from A to B because no compiler or flags are stated anywhere. The public default branch differs from the evaluated system, so treat the repo as a research artifact.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed PVLDB 18(11):3965-3978 paper that states GCC 9.4.0, C++17 and the Threadripper Pro 5995WX, but it gives no optimization flags. The public repo contains no DobLIX benchmark harness (only stock RocksDB tools) and is a RocksDB 5.1.2 tree, while the paper says RocksDB 8.1.1, so it cannot be A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Average throughput vs stock RocksDB indexing: 2.21x on read-only (RO), 1.22x read-heavy, 1.31x balanced, 1.04x write-heavy; vs TridentKV/Bourbon on RO: 1.41x/1.57x. YCSB B/C/D average 2.02x vs RocksDB; YCSB-E +42.8%. +81% vs RocksDB at 512MB cache (RO, Zipfian, AMZN). RO tail latency 2.13x better than RocksDB. Abstract: 1.19x-2.21x vs state-of-the-art methods within RocksDB. The '2.67x' figure is TridentKV's tail latency relative to DobLIX, not a throughput gain over RocksDB.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: C++17, GCC 9.4.0 (paper); optimization flags not stated in paper (repo README uses cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release; repo CMakeLists sets -std=c++11)
corrections.workload: SOSD real-world (WIKI, AMZN, FB, OSM) and synthetic (LOGN, UNI) datasets, 64M pairs with 8-byte keys and 64-byte values; RO/RH/BA/WH read-write mixes plus YCSB A-F macrobenchmarks on RocksDB 8.1.1 (per paper), 4 background threads
corrections.license: BSD-3-Clause (RocksDB 5.x-era 'BSD License For rocksdb software' LICENSE text; GitHub reports NOASSERTION) plus Facebook PATENTS file (Additional Grant of Patent Rights Version 2)
corrections.caveats: GitHub shows NOASSERTION. The LICENSE is RocksDB's old BSD-3-Clause text, shipped with Facebook's PATENTS grant (v2) and its termination clause. The public repo is a RocksDB 5.1.2 tree (include/rocksdb/version.h) with a learned_index/ directory, but the paper evaluates on RocksDB 8.1.1. It has no DobLIX-specific SOSD/YCSB benchmark scripts, and the README's './doblix' binary has no matching CMake target. Several headline ratios (1.19x, 1.41x, 1.57x) are vs other learned-index variants (Bourbon, TridentKV). The direct stock-RocksDB gains are large on read-only work (2.21x) but only 1.04x-1.31x on write-containing mixes.

notes: The paper is real, peer-reviewed and compares directly against stock RocksDB, so the 2.21x and 81% figures check out. The '2.67x throughput' claim was a misreading of a tail-latency comparison vs TridentKV. The tier drops from A to B: no flags are stated, and the public code does not match the RocksDB version the paper evaluated.

tier_reason: Only an arXiv v1 preprint (June 2024, no journal reference) by the vendor's (DiPeak) own engineers, with no public code, no compiler/flags, and an incomplete CPU model ('Intel Xeon Silver 2.40 GHz'). The claimed SIGMOD/PACMMOD 3(6) publication could not be found in Crossref's PACMMOD index, so this is first-party numbers with partial methodology.

corrections.benchmark_url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.18099 (arXiv v1 preprint, 26 Jun 2024; no journal reference listed)
corrections.claimed_speedup: YCSB (16 threads, 200M keys, 100M ops): 2.5x-4x throughput vs RocksDB and 5x-17x vs PebblesDB on point-lookup/insert workloads A, B, C, D, F. Workload A ~3x, C 2.52x, D 5.5x vs RocksDB. 50%-85% lower average/p99 latency vs RocksDB. Slower than both RocksDB and PebblesDB on scan-heavy YCSB-E. Intro: RocksDB's write amplification about 2x CompassDB's (15x in a 100M-key one-level test), read amplification 3x in pure reads, space amplification 1.2x.
corrections.hardware: Dell PowerEdge T440, Intel Xeon Silver 2.40 GHz (exact model not stated), Samsung PM9A3 3.84TB NVMe SSD, 128GB RAM, Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, ext4 (ordered mode)
corrections.workload: YCSB A-F with 16 threads after loading 200M keys (20-byte keys, 1KB values) then 100M operations; O_DIRECT, compression disabled, RocksDB/PebblesDB with 32MB LRU block cache, up to 4x128MB memtables; plus Workload C value-size sweep (50B-50KB) and fill/read/mixed microbenchmarks
corrections.caveats: No public repository: GitHub search finds only unrelated 'compassdb' projects. The arXiv preprint (v1, June 2024) has no venue or journal reference. The claimed SIGMOD / Proc. ACM Manag. Data 3(6) Article 294 publication could not be verified: there is no CompassDB entry in Crossref's PACMMOD (ISSN 2836-6573) index, even though vol 3 issue 6 is indexed. The authors are all from DiPeak, the vendor, so these are first-party numbers. The secondary baseline is PebblesDB, not SplinterDB; SplinterDB appears only as related work. Setup is not like-for-like: RocksDB/PebblesDB got a 32MB block cache under O_DIRECT, and CompassDB loses on scan-heavy YCSB-E.

notes: The '5x-17x vs SplinterDB' claim is wrong; the paper says PebblesDB. The peer-review claim is unverified (Crossref PACMMOD has no match; the ACM DL returned 403, DBLP showed a bot wall and Semantic Scholar returned 429), so the tier drops to C. Re-raise to B only if a published SIGMOD/PACMMOD version is located.
